items.question: Under what condition must a teaching be concealed rather than openly disclosed in the mortal world?
premises: A teaching is to be concealed with effort.
The mortal world is not uniformly receptive to it.
Only the lowest among men lack the fitness to receive it.
items.inference: Concealment is a measure of selective protection in an unfit setting.
uncertainties: Extent of effort required remains unspecified.
items.plain_english: What is to be concealed must be done so with effort, in the mortal world, among the lowest of men.

items.question: What qualification must a previously accomplished recipient meet before a teaching is to be given to them?
premises: A teaching is to be given only in a qualified case.
The recipient must be one previously accomplished.

items.inference: Transmission is restricted to a previously accomplished person tested over one year.
uncertainties: The nature of the test is not specified.
items.plain_english: It is to be given to one who was previously accomplished and tested for one year.

items.question: By what origin is the fifth chapter identified within this transmission?
premises: A chapter is identified by its origin.
That origin is emergence from Candradvīpa.

items.inference: The fifth chapter is the one that emerged from Candradvīpa.
uncertainties: No further content of the chapter is indicated.
items.plain_english: The fifth chapter emerged from Candradvīpa.

items.question: By what means does the speaker come to know the determination of the Kaula teaching?
premises: The speaker addresses the lord of the Kaulas.
The speaker has come to know something.
That knowledge arises by the grace of the addressee.
What is known is the determination of the Kaula teaching.
items.inference: The determination of the Kaula teaching is known to the speaker solely by the addressee's grace.
uncertainties: The prior state of ignorance is implied but not detailed.
items.plain_english: By your grace, O lord of the Kaulas, I have come to know the determination of the Kaula teaching.

items.question: What two points of inquiry must be settled to define the soul as declared in this teaching?
premises: A soul is said to be declared.
It must be asked who that soul is.
It must be asked what the nature of the soul is.
items.inference: Any account of the declared soul requires both an identification of it and a determination of its nature.
uncertainties: The answer to either question is not given here.
items.plain_english: Who is that soul that is declared? Or what is the nature of the soul?

rows.grounds: interrogative pronoun with fused sandhi as given

items.question: What must be explained about the locus of dissolution and the totality that undergoes it?
premises: Dissolution occurs in some locus.
Something goes to dissolution.

items.inference: A complete account requires stating both the locus of dissolution and all that goes to it.
uncertainties: The locus and the totality remain to be specified.
items.plain_english: And indeed, in what does it go to dissolution? Tell me all of that.

items.question: What set of attributes fixes the identity of the supreme reality being pointed to here?
premises: A single reality is indicated by 'he'.
That reality is supreme.
That reality is partless and eternal.
That reality is free from disease and stainless.
items.inference: The reality in question is defined by the conjunction of supremacy, partlessness, eternality, and freedom from affliction and stain.
uncertainties: No relation to the soul is stated in this verse alone.
items.plain_english: He is the supreme, partless, eternal, free from disease and stainless.

items.question: What identity relation holds between the soul, the haṃsa, and power as an individual?
premises: He is the soul and is supreme.
The relative clause identifies that same one.
That same one is the haṃsa.
That same one is power as an individual.
items.inference: The supreme soul is identified as the haṃsa who is power as an individual.
uncertainties: The precise distinction between 'haṃsa' and 'power as an individual' is not unpacked here.
items.plain_english: He is the soul, supreme. Indeed, he who is that is the haṃsa, power as an individual.

items.question: Where is the wind-filling air situated in relation to all beings?
premises: There is a wind-filling air.

items.inference: The wind-filling air is pervasively situated in all beings.
uncertainties: The mode of its situation is not specified.
items.plain_english: The wind-filling air is situated in all beings.

items.question: Under what minimal condition is the soul called supreme Śiva?
premises: A certain one is in question.

Upon that condition, he is called supreme Śiva.
items.inference: Merely upon leaving the body, that one is designated supreme Śiva.
uncertainties: Whether this is a designation or an ontological identity is not settled here.
items.plain_english: He, upon merely leaving the body, is called supreme Śiva.

items.question: What kind of teaching is heard abiding in the ear, addressed to the goddess?
premises: Something abiding in the ear is heard.

uncertainties: The content of that teaching is not specified.
items.plain_english: O goddess, what abides in the ear is heard as having come down through the order of tradition.

items.question: What practice over six months is enjoined for one who wears an ochre robe free from bondage?

uncertainties: The object or method of practice is not specified here.
items.plain_english: Whoever, indeed, should practice from six months wearing an ochre robe free from bondage.

items.plain_english: Freed from all diseases, he attains union together with yogis.

items.plain_english: This practice of the soul has been told to you, and to you, O Bhairavī.

items.plain_english: It is to be given to one endowed with all states, to one of resolved mind.
